REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION
TUESDAY - JUNE 9, 2026 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Community Development Department, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 2nd floor, Cerritos, CA, 90703 during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the Commission after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection at the Community Development Department during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to economic_development@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1201 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The Commission, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 4.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to economic_development@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Community Development Department no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the Commission prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Verbal comments may be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Chair extends.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the Commission, there will be no separate discussion of these items. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
COMMISSION HELD TUESDAY, JUNE 9, 2026, 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER
AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Reyes.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the Economic Development Commission were in
  attendance:

  Commissioner Alon Barlevy
  Commissioner Grace Hu
  Commissioner Aris Tagle
  Chair Alfred Reyes Jr.

4.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Chair opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Chair declared the
  public comments period closed.

5.  Consent Calendar

5A.  Approval of Minutes

  Tuesday, May 12, 2026, 7:00 p.m. Cerritos Economic Development Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes.

  MOTION: It was moved by Commissioner Hu, and seconded by Commissioner Tagle,
  to approve the Tuesday, May 12, 2026, 7:00 p.m. Economic Development
  Commission Regular Meeting Minutes.

  The motion carried (3-0-0-1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Tagle, Reyes
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Barlevy

6.  New and Old Business

6A.  Review and consideration of an informational report by the Cerritos Auto Square
  Dealers Association.

  A brief introduction was given by Economic Development Manager Kiana
  Miranda. An oral report was given by the Executive Director of the Cerritos Auto
  Square Dealers Association Tom Garrett. Mr. Garrett provided an overview of the
  Association’s role in supporting the Cerritos Auto Square, including its coordination
  with Cerritos Auto Square dealerships and their partnership with the City of Cerritos.
  Mr. Garrett continued by providing an overview of one of the City’s major commercial
 City of Cerritos  Tuesday, June 9, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
Economic Development Commission Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 3

  districts, the Cerritos Auto Square, and its significant contribution to the local
  economy. Mr. Garrett highlighted the Auto Square’s monthly vehicle sales, noting
  that approximately 4,000 vehicles are sold each month. Of those sales, roughly
  3,000 are new vehicles, and 1,000 are used, reflecting an estimated 3:1 ratio of
  new-to-used car sales. Mr. Garrett concluded by stating that car sales volume has
  gone down, and that is believed to be due to the chip shortage after the 2020
  pandemic.

  Discussion continued with the Commission regarding dealer participation in the
  Cerritos Auto Square Dealers Association, the number of staff employed by the
  Association, 2025 quarterly sales compared to 2024 quarterly sales, City of Cerritos
  and Chamber of Commerce partnership, group advertisement, and Tesla auto sales.

  The Economic Development Commission received and filed the report.

6B.  Review and consideration of an informational report regarding the fourth quarter
  2025 sales tax update for the City of Cerritos.

  A staff report was given by Economic Development Manager Kiana Miranda.
  A PowerPoint presentation of the fourth quarter 2025 (4Q 2025) public summary
  report displayed an overview of Cerritos’ financial stability and local economic
  performance across key industry sectors. Ms. Miranda continued by explaining that
  taxable sales remained consistent with previous years and that Cerritos remains a
  center of commerce and innovation.

  Discussion continued with the Commission regarding sales tax revenue, including
  HdL's analysis of sales tax data, the use of non-confidential business tax information,
  projected sales tax growth, and potential concerns affecting future revenue trends.

  The Economic Development Commission received and filed the report.

6C.  Review and consideration of an informational report regarding the 2026
  International Council of Shopping Centers (ICSC) Las Vegas Conference.

  A staff report was given by Economic Development Manager Kiana Miranda.
  A PowerPoint presentation displayed a recap for the 2026 International Council of
  Shopping Centers (ICSC) Las Vegas Conference. Ms. Miranda provided an overview
  of the conference, including keynote presentations, emerging industry trends, and
  staff's meetings with commercial real estate and hotel industry representatives. Ms.
  Miranda highlighted ongoing discussions regarding potential hotel development
  opportunities in Cerritos, business attraction efforts, outreach to prospective retail
  and restaurant tenants, and networking with regional partners to support the City's
  long-term economic development objectives.

  Discussion continued with the Commission regarding the Economic Development
  Commission's future attendance at the ICSC conference, potential new businesses in
  the City, potential locations for a hotel site, and feedback from potential tenants.

  The Economic Development Commission received and filed the report.

7.  Reports

7A.  Report from Designated Commission Staff Liaison

  There were no reports from the Designated Commission Liaison to the Economic
  Development Commission.
